messages.content:
## Responses as Code

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one JavaScript program: pass one whole, legal
JavaScript program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is evaluated verbatim, as a whole JavaScript module. Each module
below is brought into scope by a named import binding that module alone, so a
name gg prints — here, in a search hit, in a documentation view — is written at a
call site with its leading `gg.` dropped.

## Ending your session

Turns continue until you end your session.

A program that fails does not end your session: the ending it called is revoked.
Fix the fault and end your session in a program that runs to completion.

Call `gg.session.finish` with a short summary of what you did once the work is
complete.

## Your modules

Your program is given these modules:

- `gg.files`: Read, write, edit, list and search the files of the workspace. — brought into scope with `import { files } from "gg";`
- `gg.shell`: Run shell commands in the workspace. — brought into scope with `import { shell } from "gg";`
- `gg.docs`: Find a module, function or type by searching, and take a documentation view back out of the window. — brought into scope with `import { docs } from "gg";`
- `gg.views`: Show the agent a file, a value, or an entry's documentation. — brought into scope with `import { views } from "gg";`
- `gg.session`: End the session, in the one shape this agent's role produces. — brought into scope with `import { session } from "gg";`

Search the documentation to find a function, by keyword or by naming modules
above. Open a documentation view of each function you intend to call, and write
the call on a later turn.

## Messages you receive

Every message you receive is headed by one of the following labels, on its own
line — a view's label is followed by `: ` and the name it was opened under; a
file view's by `: `, its path, `:`, the 1-based inclusive line range shown and
the file's total line count — followed by a `----` rule and then the content:

- `Task` — the task you are working on, or a message from a parent agent
- `Compiler error` — your last program did not compile, so none of it ran; the message is the compiler's error and nothing else. Fix it and resend the whole program
- `Runtime error` — your last program compiled and then threw, or was stopped by a sandbox limit; the message is the error and nothing else. Whatever the program did before it threw stands, so do not repeat that work
- `Notice` — a process notice from the harness (a mode change, or guidance)
- `Summary` — a summary standing in for older turns the harness compacted out of the window
- `Documentation` — documentation or a skill you asked to read, delivered on the following turn
- `File` — a file, or a window of one, shown in your context — seeded by the run or opened by your own file-view call — headed by its path, the 1-based line range shown and the file's total line count, as `File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines` (a whole file's range runs `1-N`)
- `View` — a value your program put into your window; the view's label follows the heading, as `View: changed-files`

For example, lines 100 to 250 of a 400-line file you opened a view of arrive
as:

```
File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines
----
...those lines of the file...
```

A program that ran is not announced: the views it opened are the result.

Task
----
Create the file `notes/plan.md` in the workspace. Its required content is specified in `specs/plan-brief.md`, which is already open in your context. Write the file exactly as the brief specifies.

Documentation: gg.docs.search
----
search(options?: { query?: string; modules?: string[]; type?: string; kind?: DocKind; offset?: number; limit?: number; }): DocSearch
  options?: { query?: string; modules?: string[]; type?: string; kind?: DocKind; offset?: number; limit?: number; } — The words to look for, the filters, and the page. Every field is optional, and omitting the object entirely asks for nothing, which is the one way this call is refused.
    query?: string — The words to look for, as one string. Several specific words beat a sentence; it may be left out only when a filter says what to look at instead.
    modules?: string[] — The modules to look in, each named either the way a program writes it (`gg.files`) or by gg's own id (`files`). Exact and case-insensitive, and several are a **union** — an entry in any one of them is a hit — so one call reads the whole of the surface this agent was given. An empty list is no module filter at all.
    type?: string — One type's own name, narrowing to that type and the functions whose signatures mention it — what can be done with a value of this shape.
    kind?: DocKind — `"module"`, `"function"` or `"type"`, to see only one of them. Any other word is refused.
    offset?: number — How many hits to skip, for reading past the first page. Defaults to none.
    limit?: number — How many hits to return: 20 by default, 100 at most, and zero is refused. Compare it against `total` to see how much of the answer this page is.

Defined in `gg.docs`, brought into scope with `import { docs } from "gg";`.

Search the modules this agent holds, everything it can call, and every type their signatures name.

Best match first, and a hit is one of three things: a **module** a program imports, a function it calls, or a type a signature names. The module is what a search wants first — nothing gg offers is in scope until the program has imported the module the function lives in.

Matching is case-insensitive substring matching over names, signatures, briefs and detailed descriptions, so `docs` finds `openDocsView`. A hit whose own name matched is ranked above one that merely mentions the word in a paragraph, and the query is split on whitespace, so several specific words work better than a sentence.

Nothing here is required, the filters compose with the query and with each other, and each filter is an exact lookup rather than another thing to rank: `modules` on its own, with no query, is those modules' whole directory, which is the first hop worth making. What is refused is asking for nothing at all — no query and no filter — because a search that found nothing and a search that was never given anything to look for are different answers.

The page comes back as a value **and** opens as a view labelled `search results`, so the results can be read next turn without being shown deliberately. That view is replaced by the next search rather than accumulating.

Returns: one page of hits, best first, beside the `total` that says how much of the answer it is.

Throws `ApiError` with `invalid-argument` for a search carrying neither a query nor a filter — a search that asked for nothing and a search that found nothing are different answers — for an unrecognised `kind`, which would otherwise silently widen a search believed to be narrow, and for a `limit` of zero, which is a page that could answer nothing.

Documentation: gg.views.openDocsView
----
openDocsView(target: Function | string): void
  target: Function | string — What to document: a bound function itself, or the entry's name as a string — a module's name is its own path, as in `gg.views`.

Defined in `gg.views`, brought into scope with `import { views } from "gg";`.

Show the agent one module, function or type's full documentation: signature, description and types.

Only the types it names that have not already been shown this session are appended, so re-reading costs nothing twice. The argument is a bound function itself, as in `gg.views.openDocsView(gg.docs.search)`, or the entry's name as a string.

It is a **view** rather than a return value, so the documentation arrives in the next prompt under a `Documentation` heading and is not available in the turn that asked for it. Asking in one turn and using it in the next is the shape that works. Opening an entry that is already open does nothing at all: the band only grows, and taking a documentation view away is bought by a capability of its own.

Throws `ApiError` with `not-found` for an unknown or unbound name — searching the documentation is what says which names exist — and `invalid-argument` for an argument that is neither a function nor a string.

Documentation: gg.views.openText
----
openText(label: string, body: string): void
  label: string — What to file the view under: its selector, and what opening the same label again replaces. It may not be empty.
  body: string — What to show. An empty body is allowed: it says that something previously shown is now empty.

Defined in `gg.views`, brought into scope with `import { views } from "gg";`.

Show the agent a value the program computed, filed under a label.

A directory listing, a command's output, a child agent's answer, an assembled table: this is the channel a value takes into the next turn's context. Opening the same label again replaces what it showed, so a program may refine one view in a loop without piling up a copy per iteration.

An empty **body** is allowed, because it is how a program says that something it was showing is now empty. An empty label is not: a view with no selector could never be closed or attributed.

Throws `ApiError` with `invalid-argument` for an empty label, and `limit-exceeded`, naming the cap, when a body or a label is over gg's ceilings. Nothing is ever silently truncated.

Documentation: gg.views.openFile
----
openFile(path: string, options?: { offset?: number; limit?: number; maxLineChars?: number; }): FileRead
  path: string — The file to open, relative to the workspace or absolute.
  options?: { offset?: number; limit?: number; maxLineChars?: number; } — The window of lines to show, and how long a shown line may be; omit it to show the whole file with its lines whole.
    offset?: number — The 1-based line to start at. Omitted, the view starts at the first line.
    limit?: number — How many lines to show from `offset`. Omitted, a capped read policy's default applies, or the view runs to the end of the file. Both are honoured under every read policy.
    maxLineChars?: number — The longest a line of the view may be, in characters. Set, each line longer than it is cut there and annotated in place as `foo (123 more chars...)`; omitted, lines arrive whole. It cuts the view alone — the value this call returns and the file itself are untouched — and the byte cap is measured after the cut, which is what lets a window over a log of enormous lines fit. It must be between 1 and 65,536.

Defined in `gg.views`, brought into scope with `import { views } from "gg";`.

Read a file and show it to the agent, handing the program the same value `gg.files.readFile` does.

The split from `gg.files.readFile` is the point: that call gets bytes for the program, this one puts the file in front of the agent, so a program that reads forty files to grep them adds nothing to the window. Two pages of one file are two views that coexist, while re-opening the same page replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate.

An image file is shown as a picture, and this is the only way to look at one: `gg.files.readFile` of an image describes it without showing it.

The view's text is held to the same 65,536-byte cap a text view's body is: a window that would carry more is refused, naming the size and the bound, and nothing is opened. Nothing is ever silently truncated, so the way through is to narrow the window with `offset` and `limit`, or to cut its long lines with `maxLineChars`, in the same turn. A picture is not a text body and is bounded by gg's image cap alone.

Returns: the same value `gg.files.readFile` hands back for that window, so a program can use what it just put in front of the agent.

Throws `ApiError` with `not-found` for a path that is not there, `limit-exceeded`, naming the size and the bound, for a window whose text would be over the cap, and `invalid-argument` for a `maxLineChars` of zero or over 65,536. The read is what fails, so nothing is opened when it does.

Documentation: gg.files.FileRead
----
type FileRead = TextFile | ImageFile

Defined in `gg.files`, brought into scope with `import { files } from "gg";`.

What a read returned: a text file's window, or a picture's description.

A picture is a different kind of thing from text, so it is a different arm rather than a string that happens to be binary. The `kind` discriminant is what narrows it, and a program that treats an image as text is caught by that check instead of silently writing an empty string somewhere.

  path: string — Where to write, relative to the workspace or absolute. Parent directories are created.
  contents: string — The UTF-8 text to write. It replaces the file entirely.

Defined in `gg.files`, brought into scope with `import { files } from "gg";`.

Throws `ApiError` with `invalid-argument` for an empty path, and `io-error` when the write or a parent directory failed.

# Inventory brief

Write `notes/inventory.md` describing the workspace root.

## Required content

1. A top-level heading reading `# Workspace inventory`.
2. One Markdown list entry per entry of the workspace's top-level
   directory, in the order the listing returns them.
3. Each entry formatted as `- `, the entry's name, then ` (dir)` for a
   directory or ` (file)` for a file.

## Rules

- List the top-level directory only; do not recurse.
- Create the `notes/` directory as part of the write if it does not exist.
- Change nothing else in the workspace.

## Responses as Code

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one JavaScript program: pass one whole, legal
JavaScript program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is evaluated verbatim, as a whole JavaScript module. Each module
below is brought into scope by a named import binding that module alone, so a
name gg prints — here, in a search hit, in a documentation view — is written at a
call site with its leading `gg.` dropped.

## Ending your session

Turns continue until you end your session.

A program that fails does not end your session: the ending it called is revoked.
Fix the fault and end your session in a program that runs to completion.

Call `gg.session.finish` with a short summary of what you did once the work is
complete.

## Your modules

Your program is given these modules:

- `gg.files`: Read, write, edit, list and search the files of the workspace. — brought into scope with `import { files } from "gg";`
- `gg.shell`: Run shell commands in the workspace. — brought into scope with `import { shell } from "gg";`
- `gg.docs`: Find a module, function or type by searching, and take a documentation view back out of the window. — brought into scope with `import { docs } from "gg";`
- `gg.views`: Show the agent a file, a value, or an entry's documentation. — brought into scope with `import { views } from "gg";`
- `gg.session`: End the session, in the one shape this agent's role produces. — brought into scope with `import { session } from "gg";`

Search the documentation to find a function, by keyword or by naming modules
above. Open a documentation view of each function you intend to call, and write
the call on a later turn.

## Messages you receive

Every message you receive is headed by one of the following labels, on its own
line — a view's label is followed by `: ` and the name it was opened under; a
file view's by `: `, its path, `:`, the 1-based inclusive line range shown and
the file's total line count — followed by a `----` rule and then the content:

- `Task` — the task you are working on, or a message from a parent agent
- `Compiler error` — your last program did not compile, so none of it ran; the message is the compiler's error and nothing else. Fix it and resend the whole program

Search the modules this agent holds, everything it can call, and every type their signatures name.

Best match first, and a hit is one of three things: a **module** a program imports, a function it calls, or a type a signature names. The module is what a search wants first — nothing gg offers is in scope until the program has imported the module the function lives in.

What is refused is asking for nothing at all — no query and no filter — because a search that found nothing and a search that was never given anything to look for are different answers.

The page comes back as a value **and** opens as a view labelled `search results`, so the results can be read next turn without being shown deliberately. That view is replaced by the next search rather than accumulating.

Returns: one page of hits, best first, beside the `total` that says how much of the answer it is.

What is refused is asking for nothing at all — no query and no filter — because a search that found nothing and a search that was never given anything to look for are different answers.

The page comes back as a value **and** opens as a view labelled `search results`, so the results can be read next turn without being shown deliberately. That view is replaced by the next search rather than accumulating.

Returns: one page of hits, best first, beside the `total` that says how much of the answer it is.

Throws `ApiError` with `invalid-argument` for a search carrying neither a query nor a filter — a search that asked for nothing and a search that found nothing are different answers — for an unrecognised `kind`, which would otherwise silently widen a search believed to be narrow, and for a `limit` of zero, which is a page that could answer nothing.

Show the agent a value the program computed, filed under a label.

A directory listing, a command's output, a child agent's answer, an assembled table: this is the channel a value takes into the next turn's context. Opening the same label again replaces what it showed, so a program may refine one view in a loop without piling up a copy per iteration.

    offset?: number — The 1-based line to start at. Omitted, the view starts at the first line.

It cuts the view alone — the value this call returns and the file itself are untouched — and the byte cap is measured after the cut, which is what lets a window over a log of enormous lines fit. It must be between 1 and 65,536.

Defined in `gg.views`, brought into scope with `import { views } from "gg";`.

Read a file and show it to the agent, handing the program the same value `gg.files.readFile` does.

The split from `gg.files.readFile` is the point: that call gets bytes for the program, this one puts the file in front of the agent, so a program that reads forty files to grep them adds nothing to the window. Two pages of one file are two views that coexist, while re-opening the same page replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate.

An image file is shown as a picture, and this is the only way to look at one: `gg.files.readFile` of an image describes it without showing it.

The view's text is held to the same 65,536-byte cap a text view's body is: a window that would carry more is refused, naming the size and the bound, and nothing is opened. Nothing is ever silently truncated, so the way through is to narrow the window with `offset` and `limit`, or to cut its long lines with `maxLineChars`, in the same turn. A picture is not a text body and is bounded by gg's image cap alone.

Returns: the same value `gg.files.readFile` hands back for that window, so a program can use what it just put in front of the agent.

Throws `ApiError` with `not-found` for a path that is not there, `limit-exceeded`, naming the size and the bound, for a window whose text would be over the cap, and `invalid-argument` for a `maxLineChars` of zero or over 65,536. The read is what fails, so nothing is opened when it does.
